focus: Exodus 35 begins the building of the tabernacle after the covenant is renewed: Moses first repeats the Sabbath command, then calls for offerings from willing hearts and for skilled workers to make everything the LORD commanded. Men and women respond with gold, cloth, spun yarn, stones, and spices, and Moses announces that the LORD has filled Bezalel with His Spirit and given him and Aholiab skill and the ability to teach.

sections.title: Moses Repeats the Sabbath Command Before the Work Begins
sections.summary: Moses gathers the whole congregation and gives the LORD’s command that the seventh day be “a holy day for you, a Sabbath of rest to the LORD” (Exodus 35:2). Whoever works on it is to be put to death, and no fire is to be kindled in their dwellings on the Sabbath.

sections.title: Moses Calls for Willing Offerings and Skilled Workers
sections.summary: Moses tells the people, “Whoever is of a willing heart, let him bring it as an offering to the LORD” (Exodus 35:5), naming the materials needed. He calls every gifted artisan to come and make all that the LORD commanded, from the tabernacle and its furnishings to the holy garments for the priests.

sections.title: Men and Women Bring Their Gifts with Willing Hearts
sections.summary: Everyone whose heart is stirred and whose spirit is willing brings the LORD’s offering: gold jewelry, cloth, skins, silver, bronze, and wood, while skilled women spin yarn and the rulers bring precious stones, spices, and oil. “The children of Israel brought a freewill offering to the LORD” (Exodus 35:29) for all the work the LORD commanded through Moses.

sections.title: The LORD Fills Bezalel and Aholiab for the Work and for Teaching
sections.summary: Moses announces that the LORD has called Bezalel by name and filled him with the Spirit of God for every kind of skilled work. The LORD has also “put in his heart the ability to teach” (Exodus 35:34), in him and in Aholiab, and filled them with skill for engraving, design, embroidery, and weaving.

1.brief: Moses gathers all the congregation and says, “These are the words which the LORD has commanded you to do.” The building of God’s dwelling begins with Moses relaying God’s commands.
1.explain:
“Then Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel together, and said to them,”

After the covenant is renewed (34:10–28), Moses gathers the whole people. The building of God’s dwelling can now begin.

“These are the words which the LORD has commanded you to do:”

Moses begins with God’s commands. Chapters 35–40 record Israel carrying out what God instructed in chapters 25–31.

2.brief: Work is to be done for six days, but the seventh is “a holy day for you, a Sabbath of rest to the LORD,” and whoever works on it will be put to death. Rest comes before the work on the sanctuary begins.
2.explain:
“Work shall be done for six days, but the seventh day shall be a holy day for you, a Sabbath of rest to the LORD.”

The first command is the Sabbath. Before any work on the sanctuary begins, God’s people are reminded to rest (31:12–17). Rest comes before the work.

“Whoever does any work on it shall be put to death.”

The covenant penalty is repeated. In Israel’s setting, breaking the Sabbath was a capital offense, because the Sabbath was the sign that the LORD makes His people holy.

3.brief: Israel must kindle no fire in their dwellings on the Sabbath day. Even the holy work of building must stop for God’s rest.
3.explain:
“You shall kindle no fire throughout your dwellings on the Sabbath day.”

No fire is to be kindled on the Sabbath. Fire was needed for metalwork and cooking. Even the holy work of building must stop for God’s rest. For believers, the Sabbath points to rest with Jesus, the Lord who gives rest and makes His people holy. They are called to a deliberate weekly rhythm of resting with Him, with freedom about the day (Romans 14:5–6).
3.notes: The fire prohibition and its penalty (35:2) belong to Israel’s covenant setting.

4.brief: Moses tells the congregation, “This is the thing which the LORD commanded.” The call for gifts comes from God.
4.explain:
“And Moses spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, ‘This is the thing which the LORD commanded, saying:”

Moses relays God’s call for gifts. The call comes from God.

5.brief: Moses says, “Whoever is of a willing heart, let him bring it as an offering to the LORD,” beginning with gold, silver, and bronze. God’s dwelling will be built from willing gifts.
5.explain:
“Take from among you an offering to the LORD.”

An offering is to be taken “from among you,” from the people’s own possessions.

“Whoever is of a willing heart, let him bring it as an offering to the LORD: gold, silver, and bronze;”

Only those “of a willing heart” are to give (25:2). God’s dwelling will be built from willing gifts.

6.brief: The offering includes blue, purple, and scarlet thread, fine linen, and goats’ hair. The list repeats what God asked for in Exodus 25.
6.explain:
“blue, purple, and scarlet thread, fine linen, and goats’ hair;”

The list repeats what God asked for in 25:4.

7.brief: Ram skins dyed red, badger skins, and acacia wood are also requested. The materials for the coverings and frame are named.
7.explain:
“ram skins dyed red, badger skins, and acacia wood;”

The materials for the coverings and frame are named (25:5).

8.brief: Oil for the light and spices for the anointing oil and incense are included. The supplies for worship are named.
8.explain:
“oil for the light, and spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense;”

The supplies for worship are named (25:6).

9.brief: Onyx stones and stones for the ephod and breastplate complete the list. Every item needed is requested.
9.explain:
“onyx stones, and stones to be set in the ephod and in the breastplate.”

The stones for the priest’s garments complete the list (25:7).

10.brief: All the gifted artisans are to come and make all that the LORD has commanded. Skilled people are invited to give their work as well as their goods.
10.explain:
“All who are gifted artisans among you shall come and make all that the LORD has commanded:”

Moses calls not only for goods but for skill. “All who are gifted artisans,” literally the wise of heart, are invited to give their work.

11.brief: The artisans will make the tabernacle, its tent, covering, clasps, boards, bars, pillars, and sockets. The work begins with the structure.
11.explain:
“the tabernacle, its tent, its covering, its clasps, its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets;”

The list of work begins with the structure itself (26:1–37).

12.brief: The artisans will make the ark and its poles, the mercy seat, and the veil. The holiest furnishings are included.
12.explain:
“the ark and its poles, with the mercy seat, and the veil of the covering;”

The holiest furnishings come next (25:10–22; 26:31–33).

13.brief: The artisans will make the table, its poles and utensils, and the showbread. The furnishings of the holy place are included.
13.explain:
“the table and its poles, all its utensils, and the showbread;”

The table and its bread follow (25:23–30).

14.brief: The artisans will make the lampstand, its utensils and lamps, and the oil for the light. The light of the holy place is provided.
14.explain:
“also the lampstand for the light, its utensils, its lamps, and the oil for the light;”

The lampstand provides the light of the holy place (25:31–40).

15.brief: The artisans will make the incense altar and its poles, the anointing oil, the incense, and the screen for the door. The list reaches the entrance of the tent.
15.explain:
“the incense altar, its poles, the anointing oil, the sweet incense, and the screen for the door at the entrance of the tabernacle;”

The list reaches the entrance of the tent (30:1–10, 22–38; 26:36).

16.brief: The artisans will make the altar of burnt offering, its grate, poles, and utensils, and the laver and its base. The courtyard furnishings are included.
16.explain:
“the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles, all its utensils, and the laver and its base;”

The courtyard furnishings are included (27:1–8; 30:17–21).

17.brief: The artisans will make the court’s hangings, pillars, sockets, and the screen for the gate. The courtyard is included.
17.explain:
“the hangings of the court, its pillars, their sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court;”

The courtyard enclosure and its gate are named (27:9–19).

18.brief: The artisans will make the pegs of the tabernacle and court and their cords. Even the smallest parts are named.
18.explain:
“the pegs of the tabernacle, the pegs of the court, and their cords;”

Even the smallest parts are named.

19.brief: The artisans will make the garments of ministry, the holy garments for Aaron and his sons. The list ends with the priests’ clothing.
19.explain:
“the garments of ministry, for ministering in the holy place—the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons, to minister as priests.”

The list ends with the priests’ clothing (28:1–43).

20.brief: All the congregation of Israel departs from Moses’ presence. The people go to respond to God’s call.
20.explain:
“And all the congregation of the children of Israel departed from the presence of Moses.”

The people leave to gather their gifts. They go to respond to God’s call.

21.brief: “Then everyone came whose heart was stirred, and everyone whose spirit was willing,” bringing the LORD’s offering for the tabernacle and the holy garments. The giving flows from hearts moved to respond.
21.explain:
“Then everyone came whose heart was stirred, and everyone whose spirit was willing,”

The people come back. They give because their “heart was stirred” and their “spirit was willing.” No one is forced.

“and they brought the LORD’s offering for the work of the tabernacle of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.”

Their gifts go to “the work of the tabernacle” and “the holy garments.” The giving flows from hearts moved to respond.

22.brief: Men and women alike, as many as had a willing heart, bring all kinds of gold jewelry as an offering to the LORD. The people who once gave gold for a calf now bring gold to the LORD.
22.explain:
“They came, both men and women, as many as had a willing heart,”

“Both men and women” give. The text stresses again that their hearts were “willing.”

“and brought earrings and nose rings, rings and necklaces, all jewelry of gold, that is, every man who made an offering of gold to the LORD.”

They bring “all jewelry of gold.” Israel had given gold earrings to make a calf (32:2–4). Now the same people bring gold to the LORD for the dwelling He commanded.

23.brief: Everyone who has blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats’ hair, and skins brings them. Each person gives what he has.
23.explain:
“And every man, with whom was found blue, purple, and scarlet thread, fine linen, and goats’ hair, red skins of rams, and badger skins, brought them.”

Whatever materials people had, they “brought them.” Each person gives what he has.

24.brief: Everyone who offers silver or bronze brings it, and everyone with acacia wood brings it for the work. Every kind of material is supplied.
24.explain:
“Everyone who offered an offering of silver or bronze brought the LORD’s offering.”

Silver and bronze are brought as “the LORD’s offering.”

“And everyone with whom was found acacia wood for any work of the service, brought it.”

Those with wood bring it. Every kind of material is supplied.

25.brief: All the skilled women spin yarn with their hands and bring what they spun in blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen. Women give their skill as well as their goods.
25.explain:
“All the women who were gifted artisans spun yarn with their hands,”

Skilled women “spun yarn with their hands.” They give their labor as well as their goods.

“and brought what they had spun, of blue, purple, and scarlet, and fine linen.”

They bring the finished yarn for the sanctuary’s fabrics. Women give their skill as well as their goods.

26.brief: All the women whose hearts are stirred with wisdom spin goats’ hair. Willing hearts and God-given skill work together.
26.explain:
“And all the women whose hearts stirred with wisdom spun yarn of goats’ hair.”

Others spin “goats’ hair” for the tent. Their “hearts stirred with wisdom.” Willing hearts and God-given skill work together.

27.brief: The rulers bring onyx stones and stones for the ephod and breastplate. The leaders contribute the most precious items.
27.explain:
“The rulers brought onyx stones, and the stones to be set in the ephod and in the breastplate,”

“The rulers,” the leaders of the tribes, bring the most precious items, the stones for the high priest’s garments.

28.brief: The rulers also bring spices and oil for the light, the anointing oil, and the incense. The leaders provide for the worship of the sanctuary.
28.explain:
“and spices and oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the sweet incense.”

They also bring “spices and oil.” The leaders provide for the worship of the sanctuary. The women who spin and the rulers who bring stones all contribute to the same dwelling.

29.brief: “The children of Israel brought a freewill offering to the LORD,” men and women whose hearts were willing, for all the work God commanded. The verse sums up the people’s generous response.
29.explain:
“The children of Israel brought a freewill offering to the LORD,”

The verse sums up the response. It was “a freewill offering,” given freely.

“all the men and women whose hearts were willing to bring material for all kinds of work which the LORD, by the hand of Moses, had commanded to be done.”

The giving matched the need of “all kinds of work” that God had commanded. The people make room for the LORD’s dwelling by answering His instructions with willing hearts.

30.brief: Moses tells Israel, “See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel” of the tribe of Judah. Moses announces God’s choice of the chief craftsman.
30.explain:
“And Moses said to the children of Israel, ‘See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah;”

Moses announces publicly what God told him in 31:2. God “has called by name Bezalel.”

31.brief: God “has filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom and understanding, in knowledge and all manner of workmanship.” The Spirit equips Bezalel for the work.
31.explain:
“and He has filled him with the Spirit of God,”

God has filled Bezalel with His Spirit for this work.

“in wisdom and understanding, in knowledge and all manner of workmanship,”

The Spirit gives him “wisdom,” “understanding,” “knowledge,” and skill. The Spirit equips Bezalel for the work.

32.brief: Bezalel is gifted to design artistic works and to work in gold, silver, and bronze. His skill covers the metalwork.
32.explain:
“to design artistic works, to work in gold and silver and bronze,”

His skill covers design and metalwork.

33.brief: Bezalel is skilled in cutting jewels, carving wood, and every kind of artistic work. His gifts cover the whole range of the task.
33.explain:
“in cutting jewels for setting, in carving wood, and to work in all manner of artistic workmanship.”

His gifts cover the whole range of the task.

34.brief: God has “put in his heart the ability to teach,” both Bezalel and Aholiab of the tribe of Dan. God gives them the ability to teach others as well as to work.
34.explain:
“And He has put in his heart the ability to teach,”

God has also given “the ability to teach.” This detail is new. Bezalel can pass on his skill to others.

“in him and Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.”

The gift to teach is given to both “him and Aholiab.” God gives them the ability to teach others as well as to work.

35.brief: God has filled them with skill for engraving, design, embroidery in blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, and weaving. The leaders are equipped to direct every kind of craft.
35.explain:
“He has filled them with skill to do all manner of work of the engraver and the designer and the tapestry maker,”

God has “filled them with skill” for every craft: engraving, designing, embroidery.

“in blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine linen, and of the weaver—those who do every work and those who design artistic works.”

They can do the work and “design” it. The leaders are equipped to direct every kind of craft. The text values both hands that make and people who help others learn.
